name: Wax Plant
hook: No flowers yet? Stop cutting off the old stalks.

steps.title: Bright, out of hot sun
steps.tip: Give it bright, indirect light and shade it from hot summer sun. Too little light means no flowers.

steps.title: Let it dry between drinks
steps.tip: Let the mix dry between waterings and use room-temperature water. Water less from October to February.

steps.title: Keep it at 16–24°C
steps.tip: Aim for 16–24°C in spring and summer, away from radiators and drafts. It takes winter nights to 10°C.

steps.title: Chunky mix, snug pot
steps.tip: Mix equal parts orchid bark, peat-free compost and coarse perlite. It likes being a bit root-bound.

steps.title: Keep the old flower spurs
steps.tip: New blooms grow from old flower stalks, so never cut them off. Don't move the plant once buds form.

steps.title: Watch for mealybugs
steps.tip: Check often for mealybugs, scale and whitefly. Spider mites show up when the air is too dry.

outro: Bright light, a dry-out between drinks, and leave those spurs alone.

sources.title: NC State Plant Toolbox: Hoya carnosa
Penn State Extension: Hoyas as Houseplants

faqs.question: Why won't my hoya flower?
faqs.answer: Most don't bloom until they are 2 or 3 years old. Give it plenty of bright light, water carefully, and leave old flower stalks on, since new blooms grow from them.
